cheng_infra: Heads-up — node gpu-12 (eu-west) got drained after an Xid 13 + ECC spike. Triage took ~45m because we had to SSH and manually collect dmesg/journal and an nvidia-smi dump. Can we standardize a small collector that runs on GPU health events so we get useful bundles immediately?

sam_oncall: I hit that too. Had to run `journalctl -k -u kubelet` + `dmesg -T` by hand. A drain hook that triggers a collector would save minutes.

julie_sre: +1. Minimal bundle idea: dmesg (errors+warn), recent kernel logs, nvidia-smi query, driver info, and a small index metadata file. Keep it <20MB by default. Example collector snippet:```#!/bin/bash
OUTDIR=/var/tmp/gpu-failure-$(date +%s)
mkdir -p $OUTDIR
# kernel messages focused on recent boot and errors
journalctl -k --since "5m ago" --output=short-precise > $OUTDIR/journal-k.log 2>&1
# dmesg with timestamps and levels
dmesg -T --level=err,warn,alert,crit > $OUTDIR/dmesg.err.log 2>&1
# NV info
nvidia-smi -q -x > $OUTDIR/nvidia-smi.xml 2>&1
# small metadata index
cat > $OUTDIR/index.txt <<EOF
node=$(hostname)
collected_at=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
gpu_list=$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid,gpu_name,pci.bus_id --format=csv,noheader)
driver=$(modinfo nvidia | grep -i version | head -n1 || echo unknown)
EOF
tar -czf /tmp/$(basename $OUTDIR).tgz -C $OUTDIR .
# upload step is infra-specific (s3/r2/internal blobstore)
# curl -X PUT "https://blobstore/internal/$(basename $OUTDIR).tgz" --data-binary @/tmp/$(basename $OUTDIR).tgz
```

maria_dev: Also capture NVML counters and the GPU serial/pci slot. I had repeated XID on cards where serial was helpful to correlate rack swaps. Suggest adding `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=serial,pci.bus_id,uuid --format=csv` to index.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-214 — gpu-12 drain in eu-west. Attaching manual logs from oncall.

tomasz: We should avoid shipping full journal by default (huge). Collector should bound by time and bytes: e.g., `journalctl --since "10m ago" --lines=2000 --output=short-iso`. Also use `--rotate`/rate limit to prevent floods.

sam_oncall: I can prototype a systemd service + kubelet node-drain hook to run the collector and push a small index.json with fields: node, gpu_index, pci_id, serial, driver_version, xid_codes. Will open a PR + test on staging nodes.

deploy-bot: PR opened: https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood/infra/+/1234 — gpu-log-collector-service (sam_oncall)

julie_sre: Nice. A few policy notes: 1) scrub any potential creds in logs before upload, 2) retention defaults to 30d and TTL for non-critical events, 3) append a sha256 checksum for integrity. Also add a small failures index in our ES cluster to allow quick search by pci_id/serial/xid.

cheng_infra: Agreed on all. Action items: Sam to PR the prototype (incl systemd unit + k8s drain hook), Julie to write index schema + retention policy, Maria to add NVML counters to the collector, Tomasz to add journal/dmesg size bounds. Target: prototype on staging in 1 week. :thumbsup:

sam_oncall: I'll try to have the PR & a follow-up runbook for the oncall steps by EOD Friday. If everyone can review the PR fast we can iterate.

julie_sre: I'll add the index schema to the PR comment. Also adding a short checklist for triage: 1) check index for pci_id/serial 2) search ES for prior XID occurrences 3) compare nvidia-smi memory/power stats 4) escalate to hw if serial shows repeat failure.

cheng_infra: Perfect. Thanks — this should shave a lot of time off triage and let us correlate flaky cards across racks rather than guessing.
